edits.content:
## Mandatory answer line (write it before every answer; one line)
`Type: <noun the clue asks for> | Evidence: <quoted passage line or own fact> | Check: <candidate fits the clue's blank, is the right kind of thing, matches the clue's singular/plural, is not a clue word, and fits one distinctive clue detail (team, number, size)>`
Then the answer. If Check fails, pick another candidate. A 'Title + name' clue -> the country/organization that person leads; a quote clue -> the speaker's name (never a first name alone or a role phrase). A verbatim archive hit (Rule 3) still overrides your own knowledge. This line also serves as the check line in the strategic block; do not write two.

edits.target: - Otherwise, build the answer from passages that match several of the clue's details.
edits.content: - CONTESTANT-NAME TRAP: a name after 'right:'/'wrong:' is a contestant, never the answer, and a bare first name is never an answer. If a page repeats the clue but is cut off before any answer, it gives no answer: choose the candidate that fits every clue detail.

edits.target: asks for the title or category noun itself (Dalai Lama), not the individual named in the clue.
edits.content: - 'his / her / he / she' in a clue built around a named treaty, battle, law, deal or work ('X was signed after his final defeat at Y') asks for the PERSON behind it (who was defeated, signed or wrote it), never the treaty, battle or work already named. With 'his/her' + an office and an event, passages often list several holders of the office: pick the holder tied to the clue's event or era (check dates with your own knowledge), not the first or best-described one. Give 'First Last' with no quoted nickname or parenthetical.

- DESCRIPTOR CONFLICT: if a passage modifier on your candidate contradicts a descriptor in the clue ('freshwater' clue vs a 'sea ...' candidate, 'Atlantic' vs 'Pacific'), drop the modifier and answer with the bare standard name the passages share. When the clue says only 'this <fish/bird/tree>', give the common name, not a species from one passage. For a clue about holding a role or office, the candidate must actually have held it; a different person from the same state or party does not qualify. For 'popular'/'famous', pick the mainstream, best-known item.

edits.target: ## Rule 2: Answer the referent, not a word from the clue
edits.content: - FOREIGN WORD INSIDE THE CLUE ('Coupes A L'Ananas are desserts made with this tropical fruit'): the foreign term is an anchor. If your candidate is that foreign word or a form of it, translate it to the English name of the thing the clue asks for.

- When the clue is in English and names the generic type in English ('this Florentine palace'), give the standard English form ('<Name> Palace'), not the foreign-language form ('Palazzo <Name>'), unless the clue asks for 'the Italian/Spanish/French name of' something.

edits.target: look for the passage that glosses it ('locally referred to as lambi') and answer with the common English name (Conch).
edits.content:
- ALTERNATE-NAME clues ('...as the U.S. holiday Decoration Day', 'formerly called X', 'aka X', 'X is called / referred to as this'): the clue gives ONE name and wants the OTHER name or the generic term for the same thing. Find the passage sentence pairing the clue's term with a second name and copy that second name as written, in full standard wording. Never answer with the name already in the clue, a synonym, or a bare modifier.
- BARE DEFINITION clues (a noun phrase with no 'this', e.g. 'Sickle-shaped weapon of the Australian Aborigines'): the answer is the single TERM being defined. Find the dictionary or encyclopedia passage whose headword is glossed with the clue's own words and answer with that headword alone, without the clue's category noun.

edits.target: Give the bare name ('Ronald Reagan'), not the event, the place or the date.
edits.content:
- A clue containing a CODE or ABBREVIATION (airport code, postal or state abbreviation, chemical symbol, ticker) asks for what it stands for. Expand it and answer with the full standard name, not the letters. Text before a colon is a hint about the answer, so choose the expansion that fits it.
- A clue giving the two ends of a SCALE of technical or foreign terms ('Grades of this potable range from doux to brut') asks for the generic thing the scale classifies. Find a passage that glosses those terms together, or use your own domain knowledge. Answer with the plain product or thing, not one grade.

edits.target: copied verbatim. Use the context to pick which.
edits.content:
- Clue names sub-kinds of 'these <things>' ('the great horned & screech varieties of these birds'): the answer is the PARENT category containing all of them, in the clue's number (plural for 'these'). Never answer with one of the named sub-kinds.
- Pun, parody or tribute-act names: the clue's name only plays on the original. If the passages call it a tribute or parody, answer the ORIGINAL artist or work it riffs on, not the pun name.
- 'This team / company / country' with a player, product or policy as the descriptor: that descriptor is only an anchor. Answer the owning entity in its standard form from the passages, and check that every number, year and place in the clue fits it.

edits.target: - Ask: what category is the answer (country, person, vitamin, object, band), and what member of that category fits all the clue details?
